title: Ground-State Phase Diagram, Higher-Winding Topology, and Lifshitz Criticality in an Anisotropic Four-Spin XX Chain
authors: Mohammad Abbasi, Faraz Valeh, Saeed Mahdavifar
abstract: We investigate the quantum critical and topological properties of a spin-$1/2$ XX chain with anisotropic four-spin cluster interactions in a transverse magnetic field. The interplay of exchange anisotropy, cluster interactions, and the external field produces a rich phase diagram with multiple gapped topological phases and distinct quantum critical boundaries. We identify several Lifshitz-type transitions arising from reconstructions of the low-energy Fermi-point structure, including an unconventional multicritical point where distinct critical branches intersect and the momentum-space topology undergoes a singular reorganization. In the isotropic limit, a conventional Lifshitz transition emerges through the merging and annihilation of Fermi points, revealing distinct mechanisms of Fermi-point reconstruction within the same model. The gapped phases are characterized by quantized winding numbers $ν=0,\pm1,-2,$ and $\pm3$, with the higher-winding phases induced by the extended cluster interactions. The $ν=\pm3$ phases exhibit a richer topological structure than conventional short-range Kitaev-type chains and are separated from other sectors by field- and interaction-driven gap closings. These topological distinctions are further reflected in characteristic degeneracy patterns of the lowest levels of the bulk entanglement spectrum. Our results demonstrate that anisotropic multispin interactions provide a versatile route to realizing higher-winding topological phases and unconventional multicriticality in one-dimensional quantum systems.
summary:
This work explores the complex quantum phase diagram of a spin chain modified by anisotropic four-spin interactions. By mapping the system to fermions, the authors identify multiple topologically distinct gapped phases, including higher-winding sectors up to $|
u|=3$. This demonstrates that extended interactions offer a powerful mechanism to realize and study complex topological matter in one-dimensional quantum systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the quantum critical and topological properties of a spin-1/2 XX chain incorporating anisotropic four-spin cluster interactions under a transverse magnetic field.
main_result:
The model exhibits a rich phase diagram featuring multiple gapped topological phases characterized by quantized winding numbers up to $|
u|=3$, which are stabilized by the extended cluster interactions.
method: The analysis employs fermionization techniques, mapping the spin Hamiltonian to a quadratic fermionic form solvable via Bogoliubov transformations in momentum space.
model_or_system: The system is a spin-1/2 XX chain with nearest-neighbor XX interactions ($H_{XX}$) augmented by anisotropic four-spin cluster interactions ($H_{CI}$) and subjected to a transverse magnetic field ($h$).
key_observables:
Quantized winding numbers ($
u$), the bulk entanglement spectrum degeneracy pattern, and the ground-state energy density ($E_G$).
important_parameters: Exchange anisotropy ($J$), transverse field ($h$), and cluster interaction strengths ($\alpha,  eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the spin system to spinless fermions and analyzing the resulting single-particle energy spectrum $\varepsilon(k)$.
figures_summary: Figures schematically represent the four-spin cluster interaction Hamiltonian and show the topological phase diagram using winding numbers in the $( eta, h)$ plane, alongside the bulk entanglement spectrum for different winding numbers.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by introducing the model Hamiltonian, detailing the fermionization and diagonalization methods, and then analyzing the resulting phase diagram, topological transitions, and critical points.
why_interesting: The ability to engineer higher-winding topological phases using controllable, anisotropic multispin interactions provides a versatile theoretical platform for understanding exotic quantum states beyond standard short-range models.
